behavior.default: Routine Type-0 following writes only btMotionState.setWorldTransform, in ordinary and PMX deferred paths. Bullet applies the most recent target and derives kinematic velocities when simulation substeps execute.
behavior.zeroSubstepFrames: Native body transforms and velocities are retained. MotionState keeps the latest staged target for the next completed step. No forced simulation step is introduced.
behavior.exceptions: Construction initializes btDefaultMotionState and btRigidBody together. Explicit reset/seek/loop and Worker reconstruction synchronize native body and MotionState, clear pending inputs/forces/velocities, reset interpolation transforms/velocities and refresh bodyResults. Reset restores DISABLE_DEACTIVATION for Type-0 and ACTIVE_TAG for dynamic bodies; reset removal/reinsertion continues to clear contact caches. Warmup uses ordinary fixed-step following after reset.
behavior.layers: Helper-managed PMX post inputs retain their preceding final-layer schedule. Standalone adapters still read the current caller pose. Bone offsets, coordinate conversions and body-to-bone projection are unchanged.
behavior.dynamicBodies: Type-1 remains dynamic. PMD Type-2 position alignment and PMX Type-2 skeletal-only position handling are unchanged.
behavior.revert: Revert the Issue #88 implementation commit, rebuild the package and Examples, then deploy normally. This restores both routine native COM writes without changing the Bullet version or any solver/timestep settings. There is no runtime selector or comparison UI.

nativeBindingEvidence.binding: experiments/bullet/bindings.idl exposes btDefaultMotionState(transform) implementing btMotionState; get/setWorldTransform take native transform references. The constructor uses the default identity COM offset. Real tests execute the existing WASM export emscripten_bind_btMotionState_setWorldTransform_1 in main and Worker realms.
nativeBindingEvidence.motionStateSemantics: setWorldTransform stores the graphics transform with COM offset; getWorldTransform returns it with that offset inverted. With the exposed constructor the offset is identity. The binding copies native transforms; pooled temporary transform reuse does not lose targets.
nativeBindingEvidence.worldSemantics: stepSimulation calls saveKinematicState only when steps are requested, before the substep loop, using the clamped step count times fixedTimeStep. Kinematic MotionState is not overwritten by dynamic display synchronization on zero-step calls.
nativeBindingEvidence.bodySemantics: saveKinematicState reads MotionState into native world transform, calculates velocities from interpolation history and stores new history. setCenterOfMassTransform changes that history for kinematic bodies, so explicit reset additionally resets interpolation and velocities.
nativeBindingEvidence.babylonAssumptions: No Babylon memory layout or custom MotionState binding is used.
